description.summary: the link between crownplugind and the compositor

protocol.description:
crownplugind runs the user's themes and plugins. This protocol is how it reaches the compositor: it runs compositor actions on a plugin's behalf, hears about windows and workspaces, learns when a plugin's keybinding fires, and hands over everything the lock screen draws, because the compositor cannot read the user's files.
The global is privileged. It is only advertised to an unsandboxed client on the listener of the active, unlocked user. The lock requests are the one exception to "not while locked": they are accepted while that user's session is locked, because they carry display-only data, and their content is never shown on the login screen of another user.
crownplugind has already checked every plugin capability before it sends a request; the compositor still refuses actions no plugin may run.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_plugin_host_v1
interface.description: A single global. Binding it twice from one client is a protocol error.

entry.name: invalid_payload
entry.summary: a payload fd could not be read, or did not decode

entry.name: refused
entry.summary: plugins may not run this action, or the session is locked

request.name: watch
request.description: Replaces the set of event groups this client receives. Starts empty. Choosing windows sends a window_opened for every existing window, then a window_focused.

request.name: run_action
request.description: Runs an action written in the compositor's keybinding action grammar, e.g. "focus-workspace 2". quit, switch-vt and spawn are always refused; crownplugind spawns programs itself. Answered by one action_done with the same serial.

request.name: set_lock_scene
request.description: fd is a memfd holding size bytes: a postcard-encoded LockScene, at most 256 KiB. Every asset the scene references must have been put first.

request.name: set_lock_slot
request.description: fd is a memfd holding size bytes: a postcard-encoded view Tree for the slot named id, which the current scene must declare. Sent at most 30 times a second per slot.

request.name: put_lock_asset

description.summary: hand over an image the lock screen draws

request.description: fd is a memfd holding size bytes whose SHA-256, in lowercase hex, is id. Trees reference it as an image src of "asset:" followed by id. At most 32 MiB per asset and 64 MiB per user; the compositor checks the hash and drops assets no scene references.

event.name: plugin_action
event.description: The user pressed a chord bound to "plugin PLUGIN NAME".

event.name: lock_state

description.summary: whether the user's session is locked

event.description: Sent on bind and whenever it changes, so crownplugind can stop work nobody can see. locked is 1 when locked, 0 otherwise.

description.summary: the active workspace of an output changed
a window's app id or title changed

event.name: window_focused
event.description: id is 0 when no window has focus.
